explanation: Compared with the conjecture as described in del Pino–Kowalczyk–Wei (Ann. Math. 174, 2011; 'dkw-pnas' note) and Savin (Ann. Math. 169, 2009): bounded entire solutions of the Allen–Cahn equation Δu + u - u^3 = 0 on ℝ^n that are monotone in one direction (∂_n u > 0) have hyperplane level sets, at least for n ≤ 8. IsBoundedSolution (C^2 classical solution, bounded) matches; boundedness is equivalent to the usual |u| ≤ 1 normalisation since bounded solutions satisfy |u| ≤ 1 by the maximum principle. HasPositiveDeriv uses the first coordinate (WLOG by rotation), and HasHyperplaneLevelSets says each nonempty level set is an affine subspace of dimension n-1, the standard conclusion (equivalent to u being one-dimensional). This declaration states the single dimension n = 6, which is open (Savin proved it only under the additional limit assumption u → ±1 as x_n → ±∞). Faithful.
